name: Deterministic polynomial identity testing
question: Is there a deterministic polynomial-time identity test for general arithmetic circuits?
first_attack: Specify the field/circuit/degree model; prove a deterministic hitting set for one explicit restricted class
dispatch_next: Lock the field, the circuit shape, the degree and the oracle model in one paragraph inside the algebraic-complexity shape. Only then implement a falsifier. A checker with no declared class does not raise readiness.
dispatch_why: The campaign blocker says no circuit class is locked. A checker written before the class is fixed does not raise readiness.

campaign.hypothesis: A deterministic polynomial-size hitting set can be obtained for a named restricted arithmetic circuit class.
campaign.first_proof_obligation: State field characteristic, circuit shape, degree and oracle model, then prove the exact hitting property.
campaign.next_experiment: Implement small exact arithmetic circuits and a falsifier that searches for circuits escaping a proposed hitting set.
campaign.falsification: A nonzero circuit in the declared class vanishing at every proposed hitting-set point.
campaign.blocker: No restricted circuit class or field is locked down yet.

mentioned_in.title: Four concrete proof campaigns — first research tranche
